longform.headline: The garment acquires an identity
longform.opening: Before imagining a universal product passport, read the textile standards and trademark records that already govern product identity.

sections.heading: Then
sections.copy: China’s national standards portal records textile safety and apparel-use-information standards; these are product-governance records, not proof of a fashion-week passport system.

sections.heading: Now
sections.copy: CNIPA exposes a public trademark-search interface, but a query result must be saved and read before making any claim about a specific designer or mark.

sections.heading: Next—and the limit
sections.copy: No reviewed official source establishes that every Shanghai runway garment carries a shared digital identity, traceability record or future product passport.

longform.closing: Shanghai Fashion Week is not one technology. It is a chain of permissions that turns recognition into circulation and circulation into memory.

spokenScript: Before imagining a universal product passport, read the textile standards and trademark records that already govern product identity.
China’s national standards portal records textile safety and apparel-use-information standards; these are product-governance records, not proof of a fashion-week passport system.
CNIPA exposes a public trademark-search interface, but a query result must be saved and read before making any claim about a specific designer or mark.
The system: China textile standards, traceability and digital product data.
The object: GB 18401 textile safety record.
The honest limit: No reviewed official source establishes that every Shanghai runway garment carries a shared digital identity, traceability record or future product passport.
Enter the Shanghai evidence edition; the receipts and permissions are attached.
